llm.summary: The skill appears to be a fal.ai connector, but its read-oriented description is inconsistent with a documented account-changing queue cancellation action.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is framed as searching and reading fal.ai data, while the documented action set includes `cancel_queue_request`, which changes account/job state.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger language covers any fal.ai request, so an agent could select the skill for broad fal.ai tasks despite the manifest presenting a narrower read/search capability.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No malicious install behavior was evidenced in the supplied telemetry; VirusTotal reported 0 malicious or suspicious detections across 63 engines.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: A fal.ai connector may reasonably need access to the user's connected fal.ai account, but state-changing queue cancellation should be clearly scoped and user-directed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No evidence was supplied of hidden persistence, privilege escalation, background workers, or unrelated local data access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This does not look malicious from the available evidence, but users should understand that it can cancel fal.ai queue requests, not just search or read data. Install only if you want the agent to use this connector for fal.ai account operations, and require explicit confirmation before any cancellation or other state-changing action.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: I accept the core concern: a read/search description does not fully disclose the documented queue-cancellation capability.
[SDI-4] unexpected: I accept this as a scoping and disclosure problem rather than malicious behavior, because the mutation is at least acknowledged elsewhere in the skill text.
[SQP-1] unexpected: I accept the broad-trigger concern because `ANY fal.ai request` can cause selection for operations beyond read-only lookup.
